#2959. Kanzhun (BZ) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Pricing reform and AI efficiency drove margins as smaller clients pulled back.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:37PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Kanzhun (BZ +12.56%) management reported a period of transition in its monetization model and user expansion strategies. The company implemented a pricing reform in Tier 1 cities, replacing free job listings with a paid structure to improve listing quality and user satisfaction. Management stated that blue-collar workers and small-to-medium enterprises in lower-tier cities remain primary growth drivers, while manufacturing demand showed resilience compared to other lagging sectors like automobile and retail. Despite a reported net loss resulting from a noncash fair value adjustment on an investment, the company maintained a strong cash position and authorized an additional USD 500 million in share repurchases, reflecting a commitment to shareholder returns.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for standing by, and welcome to Kanzhun Limited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Ms. Laura Zhang, Senior Manager of Investor Relations. Please go ahead, ma'am.

Laura Zhan: Thank you, operator. Good evening, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to our third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Joining me today are our Founder, Chairman and CEO, Mr. Jonathan Peng Zhao; and our Deputy CFO, Ms. Wenbei Wang. Before we start, we would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements, which are based on management's current expectations and observations that involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors not under the company's control, which may cause the actual results, performance or achievements of the company to be materially different.

The company cautions you not to place undue reliance on forward-looking statements and does not undertake any obligation to update this forward-looking information, except as required by law. During today's call, management will also discuss certain non-GAAP financial measures for comparison purpose only. For a definition of non-GAAP financial measures and reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial results, please see the earnings release issued earlier today. In addition, a webcast replay of this conference call will be available on our website at ir.zhipin.com. With that, I will now turn the call to Jonathan, our Founder, Chairman and CEO.

Peng Zhao: [Foreign Language] Hello, everyone, and welcome to our third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. On behalf of our employees, management team and Board of Directors, I would like to thank you -- thank our users and investors for your trust and support. Let me start with our third quarter results about revenue and profitability. In the third quarter, our revenue was RMB 2.42 billion, up 11.7% year-on-year. Adjusted income from operations, excluding share-based compensation expenses, reached RMB 1.08 billion, up 19.1% year-on-year. Our adjusted operating margin rose by 2.8 percentage points year-on-year. For user growth, the number of paid enterprise customers reached 7.2 million for the 12 months ended September 30, continuing to grow both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter.

Average monthly active users, or MAU, on our app reached 73 million in the third quarter, up 14.4% year-on-year. For user achievements, the achievements that each job seeker and recruiter received on our platform remained at a high level, supported by our continued investment in matching service and product. Better outcomes in turn drove higher engagement and lower time spent on the platform. Now, let me share the pricing reform we carried out in Tier 1 cities during the quarter. We launched the Tier 1 city price experiment since the beginning of first quarter, completed the bulk of it in the second quarter, and it is now largely complete.

The reason we started it was this, in the beginning of third quarter, prior to the reform, roughly 20% of the job listing in Tier 1 cities were free, which led many recruiters seeking free exposure to place nonqualified jobs into those free slots, and that generated dissatisfaction and complaints from the job seeker side. At the same time, some ultralow-priced job listings costing as little as RMB 1 per job per day has created the escape phenomenon mentioned above. In response, we phased out free job postings in Tier 1 cities and significantly simplified our pricing tiers, setting price at RMB 4 to RMB 6 per job per day for now.

And following the reform, there will be no free lunch for job postings in Tier 1 cities, and there will be no ultralow-priced job postings as well, and that recruiter escape phenomenon has declined significantly. Throughout, we took a deliberately measured approach, rolling the experiment out gradually, testing and learning as we went, which is why it takes time, and even at prices after the completed reforms in those Tier 1 cities based on our research, there is still reasonable potential for us to be continuously tapped. Those potential could be expanded further. As long as the recruiters continue to do the recruitment on the platform, their goal is to harvest job seekers faster and more accurately.

If we continue to improve through the platform operation and technology, we can improve and provide faster and more accurate job seekers to the recruiters. Then, the average price of a job posting, which is around RMB 4 to RMB 6 per day, is actually a very low price. Since the price reform experiment, so far, the recruiter acceptance has been good. The revenue has increased and job seeker satisfaction has improved markedly, especially in those experimented areas. The constraints caused by the recruiter escape have decreased significantly as well. Going forward, the company will be very cautious to explore those similar projects and opportunities in other suitable places.

Thirdly, in Tier 2, Tier 3, Tier 4 and Tier 5 cities, user growth remains the main thing driving the company's revenue growth. Statistically, in the third quarter, the revenue contribution proportion from the Tier 3 and lower-tier cities rose by nearly 2 percentage points year-on-year, driven mainly by the faster user growth. Based on our credible research, those -- the vast majority of these users were the first time to use the online recruitment services. In other words, with the help of BOSS Zhipin, many customers and recruiters in the third-tier cities and lower-tier cities have gradually realized the digitalization and online recruitment behavior.

That is since our online services was launched in July 2014, it has traveled with millions of recruiters in China's first-tier cities. China has more than 400 million urban workforce and more than 40 million active enterprises. A lot of them are located in the Tier 2, 3, 4 and 5 cities. And so we should maintain growth and penetration of users in those areas, and that will bring us a new business model and the growth of our revenue, and that provides ample room for us to grow. Fourthly, our company's progress in advancing the application and development of AI technology.

The blue-collar users and new workers in the company communicating with AI enable the platform to better understand their needs, and thereby, we can serve them better. What we have discussed here is the AI-driven product that we have mentioned earlier called Zhishanshan. The feature of these products is that it supports users to communicate with AI for multiple rounds. Its purpose is to better obtain the user information from the communicated results and put some information and knowledge known to the platform.

There are actually a lot of blue-collar users, and the newcomers of workplace in their text information and communication, in fact, they do not have sufficient content that, that can be supported by our recommendation system in order to provide the recommendation results. The users who use Zhishanshan, actually, they can receive a higher achievement rate. And the proportion of achievements is what -- is actually several digits higher in percentage than the other users that are not using Zhishanshan. The next thing to AI is that some recruiters who are more experienced and know more clearly about what kind of people they really want to hire make greater use of the AI search functions.

And the feature of this product is that user can input long text to express what they actually want. That is something that the traditional search queries cannot support. That is a simple methodology. AI search can better meet their needs. Statistically, more users are using the AI search functions. And so they have a follow-up of like 40% of their chats are initiated in the AI search scenario. We certainly will provide hunting consultants with a specific agent to help them find suitable candidates within our talent pool. And now, we actually have more than 7 million monthly active users, and we can also call them active job seekers.

In addition, we have a larger talent pool of job seekers that have not expressed their intention on the platform for the time being. So we call them as the passive job seekers. And in fact, if you are not able to like find those job seekers accurately, the things become very troublesome. But if it is accurate, both sides can still be like very happy, and there is the agent doing a good job with this method. And the agent is welcomed by our hunting consultant experiment team.

And with the assistance of this agent, the first interview rate of the candidates recommended by the consultants and also accepted by our clients increased by 50%, and it is a good technical achievement in our AI-driven closed-loop business. Fourth, we provide specific clients with the AI-supported batch recruitment needs. The company provides configurable job posting, talent screening, automated invitation processing, preliminary assessment, AI interview and post-interview summaries, directly delivering suitable candidates to clients and meeting our customers' recruitment needs for under the situation that we can serve those recruitments -- recruiters with a large number of candidate recruitment needs and also with strong timeliness, and this actually achieved success.

And we will be further -- and this function will be further improved. And from the AI science perspective, we have maintained a cautious investment and are still working on the small model development that we previously had. So in this October, we released Nanbeige4.3-33B, a model we developed in-house. It outperforms comparable open-source models in the 30 billion parameter class on multiple benchmarks, including coding, office agent tasks and general reasoning. Artificial Analysis, a model evaluation organization, ranked it as the best overall open-source model with fewer than 40 billion parameters. Finally, let me discuss our shareholder returns. Today, the Board passed a resolution approving the company's latest share repurchase program.

On top of the USD 400 million share repurchase program, which we approved in March 2026, we announced a new share repurchase program and increased the share repurchase amount by USD 500 million over the next year. Last quarter, we paid our annual dividend of USD 230 million. So far this year, we have also repurchased over USD 300 million of our shares, representing nearly 5% of our total share capital. To date, total shareholder return through the repurchase and dividends have exceeded USD 530 million, which is more than 100% of our last year's adjusted net income.

The new USD 500 million repurchase authorization shows that, first, it actually reflects our confidence in the company's sustained long-term growth even in a challenging external environment. And also -- it also -- it actually represents that the management and the Board are committed to deliver more than we promised on shareholder returns over time. That concludes my remarks. Our Deputy CFO, Wenbei, will now walk you through our financial results in detail.

Wenbei Wang: Thanks, Jonathan. Hello, everyone. Now, let me walk through the details of our financial results of the third quarter of 2026. We delivered another resilient quarter marked by healthy revenue growth and further improved profitability. Revenue for this quarter was RMB 2.42 billion, up 12% year-on-year, with contributions from both user growth and improved monetization. The paying ratio among active enterprise users improved for the fifth consecutive quarter. Number of paid enterprise customers increased by 6% year-on-year to 7.2 million over the trailing 12 months ended September 30, 2026. ARPPU growth accelerated in this quarter, underpinned by a combination of enhanced service capabilities and reforms to our monetization model. Key accounts sustained strong growth momentum supported by deeper service engagement.

Moving to the cost side. Our total operating costs and expenses increased by 7% year-on-year to RMB 1.6 billion this quarter. In this quarter, we sponsored the FIFA World Cup and the WorldSkills Competition. Meanwhile, we increased our investment in AI-related cloud services. Despite all those investments, our profitability continued to improve. Excluding share-based compensation expenses, our adjusted operating margin expanded by 2.8 percentage points year-on-year to a record high of 44.5%. This was primarily driven by our strong operating leverage, disciplined execution and ongoing efforts to enhance operating efficiency through AI applications. Looking into each segment, cost of revenue increased by 5% year-on-year to RMB 324 million this quarter.

This increase was mainly due to higher server and bandwidth costs, partially offset by the App Store commission fee because Apple lowered the commission ratio and improved operating efficiency as we widely leverage AI in our daily operations, verifications, customer services. As a result, our gross margin stayed at a healthy level of 87%. Sales and marketing expenses increased by 49% year-on-year to RMB 585 million this quarter, mainly due to the marketing campaign we just mentioned, as well as an increase in sales employee-related expenses related to higher cash revenue. Our R&D expenses were RMB 425 million this quarter, up 4% year-on-year.

Excluding share-based compensation expenses, our adjusted R&D expenses increased by 6% year-on-year to RMB 350 million, mainly due to higher cloud service fees and server depreciation costs related to AI infrastructure investments. Our G&A expenses decreased by 34% year-on-year to RMB 241 million this quarter, mainly due to the one-off impairment of intangible assets recorded in the same period last year. Excluding the impairment, G&A expenses were relatively stable. Interest and investment recorded RMB 1.3 billion loss this quarter against RMB 228 million of income 1 year ago, mainly due to an approximately RMB 1.4 billion noncash fair value changes of one of our invested companies.

Income tax was a benefit of RMB 161 million this quarter compared with an expense of RMB 172 million a year ago. This shift reflects a noncash deferred tax benefit of RMB 361 million arising from the same investment loss described above, which more than offset our normal tax on operating profits. As a result, net income was a loss of RMB 249 million this quarter, driven by this noncash fair value adjustment. Despite the year-on-year growth in income from operations, excluding the above-mentioned investment loss, the related deferred tax benefit and share-based compensation expenses, adjusted net income was RMB 1.1 billion, up 12% year-on-year. Net cash provided by operating activities was RMB 1.3 billion this quarter.

As of June 30, 2026 (sic) [ September 30, 2026], our cash position, including cash, cash equivalents, short-term time deposits and short-term investments, both excluding -- but excluding investments in equity securities, stood at RMB 19.6 billion. Our strong cash position and cash-generating capability enable us to sustainably deliver our shareholder return commitment. As Jonathan just mentioned, today, our Board of Directors has authorized a new share repurchase program on top of the existing one, which effective from November 25, 2026, for a 12-month period, under which we may purchase additional up to USD 500 million of our shares, further reflecting the determination of the management to continue delivering shareholder return commitments.

And now for our business outlook, given the challenging recruitment demand trend for the fourth quarter of 2026, we expect our total revenues to be between RMB 2.19 billion and RMB 2.23 billion, a year-on-year increase of 5.3% to 7.3%. That concludes our prepared remarks. And now we would like to take -- answer questions. Operator, please go ahead.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] First question comes from the line of Timothy Zhao of Goldman Sachs.

Timothy Zhao: [Interpreted] It's a pleasure to see that we increased our shareholder commitment against this environment. I have 2 questions. One is, can management share what is the latest recruitment industry trend since third quarter this year to date? And what is the detailed trend by industry, by enterprise scale and by blue collar versus white collar? And secondly, could management elaborate how these changes reflect in your outlook in the fourth quarter revenue? And what is our observation on the market competitive landscape? And what is our solutions in order to grow the business in this environment?

Peng Zhao: [Interpreted] Thank you, Tim, for your question. So yes, we have observed that entering into the fourth quarter, the overall recruitment demand is challenging and especially the supply and demand situation, which showed more job seekers comparing to enterprise users, and this trend is still continuing. So this gives us quite a challenge to provide better service and satisfying service to more of our users. And if you look at details, so we saw that the change in magnitude from the small and medium-sized enterprises is bigger and also combined with the seasonality considerations because December is normally a low season.

So approaching the end of the year, the job seeker normally want to switch a job, and the recruiters were slowing down their recruiting activities. The bigger, larger companies performed the relatively more resilient because from 2 aspects: first, it will continue to finish its previous recruitment plan. So they still continue to do the recruiting activities. Another aspect is a lot of bigger enterprises will sign annual contract for the next year from October to December. So this signing activities is basically normal. From a blue and white collar perspective, the blue-collar users and revenue contribution further improved because we have better user growth and penetration among the blue-collar users.

And in the third quarter, the revenue contribution from blue-collar users increased by 1.5 percentage points year-on-year. One of noteworthy background here is that BOSS Zhipin was actually a white-collar-oriented platform from the beginning and in fact, but now we have gradually become more and more blue over these years. But the penetration rate of the whole blue-collar users are still on a fast-growing process. So we can understand this blue-collar penetration story will continue to drive our overall growth. From an industry perspective, the manufacturing industry continued to lead the growth.

In third quarter and the fourth quarter till today, the newly added job posting among manufacturing industry grew more than double digits year-on-year and the relatively lagging industries, including like automobile, finance, advertising and retail. So I understand this topic coming from the most concentrated concern of our company, which is growth. So actually, I have 3 wheels on our hand. The first one is in the lower-tier cities, we will continue the user penetration growth as our main engine.

And then in the other top-tier cities and some of the second-tier cities, the monetization reform, which main purpose is to reduce the escape and massive user complaints have achieved the initial success, so which enable us to further push forward this price reformation in the higher penetrated cities to increase our revenue growth. And the third one is a relatively smaller wheel, but it is also ongoing. So under the support of our technology, we are able to provide massive hiring -- fast massive hiring for bigger clients. So providing a very comprehensive service to deliver directly suitable candidates. This one is quite with strong certainty.

Another one is even smaller wheel, but we also see some silver lining that with the support of AI, we have provided very good service for our internal headhunter consultant to use undeveloped massive user resources to provide comprehensive service for complicated customers. So all these things are under normal operation. And back to the fourth quarter outlook, which you confirmed, given all those circumstances, we have a relatively cautious one. So from our historical pattern, we will deliver what we promised, and we will strive to even deliver better. So that's what we were working on. So to sum up, we are under different challenges, but still we have been optimistic for long term.

That's our answer for this question. And now, let's move on to the next one.

Operator: Next we have Eddy Wang from Morgan Stanley.

Eddy Wang: [Interpreted] During the prepared remarks, you mentioned that we have launched the pricing lift experiments in Beijing, Shanghai starting in the third quarter. Can you share more feedback from these recruiters? And how should we think about the pace of the future price increase and the impact on the long-term revenue growth? And the second question is, can you elaborate on the application of AI-enabled products and the closed-loop services? And what's the implication for our future pricing strategy and the revenue growth road map?

Peng Zhao: [Interpreted] I understand your concern about our customer reaction during our price reform in the first tier cities. This is the things we concern the most because our clients have paid money, paid time and patience. If he trusted this platform more, he also paid a cost of opportunity. My understanding is the customer is looking for a quick and -- quick candidates, which also suit him. So based on this understanding of our customers, now we are setting the price of our products on RMB 4 to RMB 6 per day in place like Beijing and Shanghai.

The meaning behind that, which means if I can give you 15 super candidates each month, then you are only paying us RMB 8 to RMB 12 for each super candidate. I think this is a very, very low price. So based on this judgment and understanding of the industry during our reform, we -- as we expected, there is no real user attrition, for example, more than 2% who showed that they will never use our platform again. So this is -- like this reform achieved success under our cautious control. In fact, we're also confident to invest more resources to better understand our clients who are still willing to hire.

But before they invest their time and patience and internal communications, we can better satisfy our clients, give them better results, so they were willing to pay us more for valuable service. Beijing is the first to accomplish this experiment, and we saw very positive results. And now we also finished our experiment for the first-tier cities. So we are confident that all this added together we will have positive impact and also another way to maybe to balance some of the lower season and impact -- external impact. And also about this AI, I just shared quite a lot during my remarks. But also currently, there are several things -- have definitely ongoing.

First, our client is using a lot of search function. So a lot of people are using search to do long text communication interaction so they can achieve better results from us. And some of very large clients use us like one-stop, we can call it a one-stop service, including assessing, communication and delivery. And this service is also going well. And also our internal consultant using our products to help them to better find candidates through our candidate pool to external people. All this together and including the price reformation we might perform in the second-tier cities and the products we have going out, all will gradually contribute to our business revenue growth next year.

And that's our answers to the second question. Let's move on to the next one.

Operator: Next, we have Wei Xiong from UBS.

Wei Xiong: [Interpreted] First, based on the current trends of high-end demand, what's our plan for investment in CapEx and other initiatives next year? And how should we think about the long-term margin level? And second, we noticed the new share repurchase program. So just wondering, could management share your thoughts around shareholder returns and payout ratio for next year?

Peng Zhao: [Interpreted] So thank you about our plan for investment. The first -- there are several directions. First is companies still want to try out our model to the country and district relatively friendly or more neutral to serve more clients and gain achievements. So that's one direction. The second is if some investment can further enhance our capability on matching recommendation, and also, our super price, who are willing to consider. So those 2 directions are quite clear. So one is on global and one is on recommendation. And on the CapEx front, we will focus more on our AI application.

But for the pretraining model investment, we will be constrained, and we definitely will not do any kind of competition of GPUs or [ matrix arms ]. And the margin, we will maintain relatively stable and may slightly increase and that can last longer term. Yes. And for the shareholder return on the payout ratio, so you can see we have very healthy and abundant cash reserve. We have overdelivered our promised 50% of shareholder return. At the beginning of this year, we actually did 100%. This USD 500 million new program, and also, we have some left. So together, we have almost USD 600 million total buyback quota over the next 12 months.

So we can expect the company will continue to overdeliver the shareholder return commitment and create value for our shareholders. And that's our answer to the third question. And given the time constraint, we can only take one last question, operator.

Operator: Next, we have Thomas Chong from Jefferies.

Thomas Chong: [Interpreted] Can management share about the progress for OfferToday and other overseas initiatives? What are our strategies entering the new market, the preliminary spending and KPI that can be shared?

Peng Zhao: [Interpreted] Thank you for your interest in OfferToday, which is our -- initially, it's actually an experiment in Hong Kong, China, but now we have -- find it, it actually went quite successful. From an app perspective, OfferToday -- online recruitment and job seeking app perspective, OfferToday have taken the #1 position in Hong Kong for quite a while. But it still take us longer term to learn how to use Cantonese, English and local slang to express information of job content and recruitment from excellent powerful local job seekers and local customers and grew alongside with us.

And another app also called OfferToday in the near future will also appear in Singapore, but it also will take a longer term to adapt how to better serve the local customers. And on our globalization, actually, we have a thinking matrix. That is we are willing to looking at one place or one city, whether they have a chance in 5 or in 10 years to realize the similar revenue size of -- which we see like Beijing and Hangzhou in 2 years. For example, Beijing, we are assuming they have like USD 150 million market size, Hangzhou maybe USD 100 million.

So if they have this kind of market potential, that's something which is worth spending time and money to invest. And on the other side of this metric is time. We simply divided into 5 years and 10 years 2 cycle. So if a 5-year investment, if we can see a similar size of Hangzhou, then we assume that's complying with our view on Hong Kong and -- China, Hong Kong and Singapore. And in fact, we find a lot of place who have -- or cities have similar opportunities, and we are willing to do similar investment. Also, last time I reported to you with a 5-year potential, and we call that middle dish.

And if a place takes 10 to 15 years' time to achieve similar scale, we're calling it like -- more like a slow dish. That's how we do it. We will document internally on how we'll invest our money and human resources. So I just fully shared with you the simple matrix. And that's all of our answers to today, and we can conclude today's call, operator.

Operator: Due to time constraints, that concludes today's Q&A session. At this time, I will turn the conference back to Laura for any additional or closing remarks.

Laura Zhan: Thank you once again for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please contact our IR team directly. Thank you. [Portions of this transcript that are marked [Interpreted] were spoken by an interpreter present on the live call.]

#2957. 19 Business Upgrades To Maximize The Value Of Real-Time Payments

As instant-payment networks such as FedNow and the RTP network reach more financial institutions, more businesses have the opportunity to send and receive funds within seconds, even on weekends and holidays. However, taking full advantage of that speed requires more than gaining access to a new payment network. Legacy workflows built around batch processing and traditional banking hours can create delays and operational gaps even when money moves instantly.

For many companies, the transition to real-time payments will require a fresh look at the internal technology and business practices that support financial operations. Below, Forbes Technology Council members share ways companies can modernize their systems and processes to make real-time payments more efficient, secure and beneficial to the business.

Update ERP payment reconciliation and the capacity behind it. From my experience leading fintech integration projects, connecting payment channels is only part of the work. Internal systems must confirm transactions, update balances and flag duplicates at any hour. Adopt API-driven, automated reconciliation with exception handling, and load-test it at peak volume without maintenance windows. - Mohammad Sharif Daoud, Global Center for AI Excellence

Combine automated matching with clear ownership of exceptions. Routine transactions should reconcile automatically, while unmatched payments, short payments and missing remittance details are routed to accountable teams for timely resolution. This approach reduces manual effort, improves visibility into available cash, and helps finance teams put incoming funds to work sooner while resolving discrepancies faster. - Venus Garg, Elevance Health

Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Providers and participants in the expanding instant payments ecosystem must modernize risk assessment alongside payment infrastructure. Instant settlement leaves little room for error, while added verification and manual review undermine speed. Richer financial data and streamlined fraud, liquidity and other risk assessments can enable more instant payments without sacrificing sound controls. - Brian Reshefsky, EDGE

Companies should modernize their treasury and cash management systems. Real-time payments mean little if reconciliation, liquidity management and reporting remain outdated. Integrating automation, AI-driven forecasting and real-time financial visibility enables businesses to optimize cash flow, reduce risk and make faster, smarter capital decisions. - Paul Kerslake, N3XUS

Payment routing deserves more attention. Many companies choose how to send money based on fixed bank relationships or manual processes. Connecting internal systems to multiple payment networks lets them route each payment based on cost, availability and whether the recipient can receive it instantly. That makes real-time payments useful across the business instead of within a single network. - Maghnus Mareneck, Cosmos Labs

I’d modernize how procurement negotiates supplier payment terms. If a company can pay immediately upon verified delivery, procurement should be able to negotiate something in return, such as a discount, better pricing or priority access to inventory. That requires procurement and finance to agree on when using cash sooner is worthwhile. The opportunity is to make payment speed part of the negotiation. - Kacee Johnson, radical

Fraud detection and payment authorization need to evolve with real-time payments. When money moves instantly, there’s little time to detect fraud or reverse a transaction. Companies need real-time fraud analysis and stronger verification that a payment was genuinely authorized by the customer, without slowing down legitimate transactions. - Alex Spokoiny, Check Point Software

Update cash and liquidity management. When payments settle around the clock, including weekends, treasury can’t rely on end-of-day positions and cutoff times. Modernize to real-time cash visibility and automated funding of accounts so you can pay and collect any time without tying up idle balances. - Aruna Veerappan, Upwork Global Inc.

Customer-facing billing and refund workflows should be modernized to take full advantage of real-time payments. Many companies still rely on multi-day settlement, batch disbursements and manual refund processes that frustrate customers accustomed to instant transactions. Modernized workflows deliver instant payouts, real-time refunds and transparent payment status, improving customer experience and loyalty. - Nitin Agarwal, Luminace

Companies should modernize how they track incoming payments. What’s the point of receiving money in seconds if accounting takes two days to recognize it? It’s like getting a package delivered instantly but waiting until tomorrow to open the door. Real-time payments need real-time accounting. - Margarita Simonova, ILoveMyQA

Companies should modernize their payment approval workflows to keep pace with instant-payment networks. If a supplier payment still waits until the next business day for approval, the money may move instantly, but the business hasn’t gained much. Setting approval limits and delegating authority in advance lets routine payments go through around the clock, while larger or unusual transactions still get reviewed before funds leave the account. - Elton Chan, Second Talent

Modernize the payment decisioning and exception-management architecture. Real-time settlement atop batch-era fraud controls, liquidity monitoring, reconciliation and exception handling merely accelerates operational risk. 24/7 money movement demands 24/7 intelligence, controls and accountability. Speed without trust is a liability. - Rajjie Sarmey, FutureProof CXO™

Companies should modernize their liquidity orchestration layer, not just payment gateways. Real-time payments require real-time intelligence across treasury, fraud detection, reconciliation and cash forecasting. The next frontier is agentic liquidity management, where AI continuously anticipates cash needs, dynamically allocates funds and optimizes working capital. Instant settlement should enable instant financial decisions. - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC

Real-time payments won’t automatically create value. I’d challenge the premise that modernizing one process or internal system is enough. Companies need to assess technical debt, process debt and data debt together. Money can move instantly while the business operates on yesterday’s information. The question leaders need to focus on is whether the entire organization can access and act on that data. - Neda Nia, Stibo Systems

Modernize how you approve and double-check payouts before money goes out the door. Older payment methods gave finance teams until the end of the day to catch a duplicate invoice, a wrong account or a bad refund before the bank processed it. With instant payments, the money is gone in seconds, so your approval rules and mistake checks have to happen up front, before anyone clicks “Send.” - Vatsal Bhardwaj, Jabali.ai

Update collections and customer communication. If payment status reaches the CRM overnight, customers who paid at 9 a.m. still get an overdue reminder at noon. At one client, about one in 10 dunning emails went to accounts that had already paid. Streaming payment events into Salesforce stopped those messages, cut “I already paid” support cases by roughly 35%, and released credit holds the same day. - Sergii Grushai, Peeklogic

Modernize tax determination and allocation. When a customer pays instantly, the company should reserve sales tax, VAT and withholding by jurisdiction and legal entity. Many firms calculate these obligations later from batch reports, overstating available cash and rushing remittances. Link payment events to tax rules and entity records, then test reversals and partial payments so speed does not create a compliance backlog. This clearly separates cash from tax owed. - Jagadish Gokavarapu, Wissen Infotech

Your customer service layer needs modernization. Here’s why: Real-time payments are final. There’s no recall window. So the “Here’s my money, can I cancel it?” questions spike, and they need answers in seconds, not tomorrow. In our banking data, payments and money movement drive roughly 36% of guided-task volume. Instant money needs instant, accurate answers. - Merlin Bise, Inbenta

Companies should integrate instant-payment networks directly with their ERP or through treasury platforms, ensuring cash inflows and outflows are reflected in real time. Payment initiation, status updates, and automated AR and AP matching can enable straight-through processing, reduce manual intervention and improve cash visibility. This aligns financial operations with payment speed, improving efficiency and working capital management. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics
